inputs.coverage: Published triaxial figure from the 2019 September 8 multi-chord stellar occultation: semiaxes 126 ± 22, 109 ± 19 and 68 ± 13 km, volume-equivalent radius 98 ± 17 km (Braga-Ribas et al. 2023, A&A 676, A72). Only the apparent limb ellipse is fitted from the chords. The third axis follows from three stated assumptions: a Jacobi fluid-equilibrium figure at the 5.917813 h rotation period, the true light-curve amplitude 0.16 ± 0.03 mag of Groussin et al. 2004, and a body pole assumed equal to the Ortiz et al. 2015 ring pole. The area-equivalent radius was held fixed at 105 (+6/-7) km, the radiometric value of Lellouch et al. 2017, so the scale is radiometric, not occultation-measured. This is a model figure, not resolved terrain. Illustrative ICRF north pole (right ascension 0 degrees, declination +90 degrees), arbitrary prime meridian and phase. Chiron has no measured spin pole. The published ring or disk pole near ecliptic longitude 151 degrees, latitude +20 degrees is a pole of the surrounding material; the shape paper assumes the body shares it, and this display does not adopt that assumption as an orientation. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
